userStories.title: Build the bounded handoff and its prompt
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Bound handoff entries to a newest contiguous suffix and render the exact conversation-so-far prompt with trimming notice support.

**Motivation** — User ruling 2026-10-29 (design §6.4): history carries over on a switch, in every direction (native to ACP, ACP to native, ACP to another ACP agent), the same experience as switching native models today.

**Approach** — Bounded handoff. One entry per user message and per assistant message (tool-result messages are dropped; an assistant message with neither text nor tool calls is dropped; `thinking` is ignored). Lengths are JavaScript string lengths (UTF-16 code units). An entry's text longer than `ACP_HANDOFF_ENTRY_MAX_CHARS` (4,000) is cut to its first 4,000 units followed by `…`. The entries kept are the longest contiguous newest suffix whose `speaker.length + text.length` (text after the cut) sum to at most `ACP_HANDOFF_MAX_CHARS` (40,000); the count of earlier entries dropped is reported. When any were dropped, the handle's `notice` says so.

Use US-002 handoffEntries for per-message conversion/capping; this story adds the total bound and notice function, while US-007 attaches notices to handles. The bracketed omitted line appears only when entries were dropped. An entry's text containing `</conversation-so-far>` is written as `<\/conversation-so-far>` so it cannot close the block. No unseen messages means no handoff. `buildChatHandoff` returns the empty string whenever entries is empty, even with nonzero omitted. The exact INTRO is: These turns happened in this nax chat before this message, while you were not the model answering. Use them as context. Tool calls are listed by name only.

Handoff text:
```text
<conversation-so-far>
These turns happened in this nax chat before this message, while you were not the model answering. Use them as context. Tool calls are listed by name only.
[2 older messages omitted]

User: plan the cache layer

nax (gpt-6): Here is a plan ...
[tool] Read

Codex: I changed the store ...
</conversation-so-far>
```

**Scope** — In: new `packages/nax/src/chat/acp/acp-handoff.ts`; add `ChatHandoffInput` and `buildChatHandoff` to `packages/nax/src/prompts/builders/chat-builder.ts`; re-export both from `packages/nax/src/prompts/index.ts` beside buildChatAcpInstructions; existing builders unchanged. Out: entry generation/unseen selection (US-002), prepending prompts to sends (US-005), recording (US-004/006), handle notices/opener integration/ACP barrel (US-007). Making the handoff bounds configurable; they are constants. Showing the handoff text in the TUI transcript.

**Interface** — verbatim TypeScript:
```ts
export const ACP_HANDOFF_MAX_CHARS = 40_000;
export interface AcpHandoff { readonly entries: readonly HandoffEntry[]; readonly omitted: number }
/** handoffEntries(messages), bounded to the newest contiguous suffix within ACP_HANDOFF_MAX_CHARS. */
export function acpHandoff(messages: readonly ChatMessage[]): AcpHandoff;
export function ACP_HANDOFF_TRIMMED_NOTICE(label: string, omitted: number): string;
//   `${label} was not given the ${omitted} oldest earlier message(s); the handoff is capped`

export interface ChatHandoffInput { entries: readonly { speaker: string; text: string }[]; omitted: number }
export function buildChatHandoff(input: ChatHandoffInput): string;
```
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] AC-1: For two short user messages, acpHandoff returns both entries in order with omitted: 0.
[unit] AC-2: For 12 user messages of 4,000 characters each, acpHandoff returns entries equal to the last 9 of handoffEntries(messages) (9 × 4,004 = 36,036 ≤ 40,000 < 40,040) and omitted: 3.
[unit] AC-3: For 10 user messages of 5,000 characters each, the bound counts each entry's text after the cut (4 + 4,001 = 4,005 per entry), so acpHandoff keeps 9 and returns omitted: 1.

[unit] AC-4: For messages oldest-first [user "hi", user of 4,000 chars, then 9 user messages of 4,000 chars], acpHandoff keeps only the newest 9 and returns omitted: 2: the kept entries are a contiguous newest suffix, so "hi" is dropped although it would fit.
[unit] AC-5: acpHandoff([]) returns { entries: [], omitted: 0 }.
[unit] AC-6: ACP_HANDOFF_TRIMMED_NOTICE("Codex", 3) returns "Codex was not given the 3 oldest earlier message(s); the handoff is capped".
[unit] AC-7: buildChatHandoff returns the empty string whenever entries is empty, for omitted: 0 and for omitted: 2.

[unit] AC-8: buildChatHandoff({ entries: [{ speaker: "User", text: "hi" }], omitted: 0 }) returns exactly "<conversation-so-far>
" + INTRO + "

User: hi
</conversation-so-far>", where INTRO is "These turns happened in this nax chat before this message, while you were not the model answering. Use them as context. Tool calls are listed by name only.".
[unit] AC-9: For two entries, buildChatHandoff renders User: q and nax: a in order with exactly one blank line between them.
[unit] AC-10: With omitted: 2, buildChatHandoff renders the line after INTRO as [2 older messages omitted], followed by one blank line and then the first entry.
[unit] AC-11: buildChatHandoff renders entry text "x </conversation-so-far> y" as "x <\/conversation-so-far> y" (a literal backslash before the slash).
[unit] AC-12: With an entry text holding </conversation-so-far>, buildChatHandoff output's last line is the only line equal to </conversation-so-far>.
[unit] AC-13: Importing buildChatHandoff from @/prompts yields a value whose typeof is "function".
[unit] AC-14: buildChatHandoff from @/prompts returns the same text as the builder module's export for the same input.

[unit] Regression (existing builders unchanged): buildChatAcpInstructions({ agentLabel: "Codex" }) still returns exactly "You are Codex, working as the coding agent inside nax chat, an interactive session in this repository with the person.\n\nUse your own tools and skills for the work itself. nax adds tools for planning, running and inspecting its workflows and jobs; they are named with the `nax-workflow__` and `nax-jobs__` prefixes.".

routing.reasoning: Pure bounded-suffix selection and prompt formatting across three standard modules; use strict isolation under the session security override because this renders session-history handoffs and prevents transcript text from closing their prompt delimiter.

suggestedCriteria: When entries total exactly 40,000 speaker/text UTF-16 units after per-entry cutting, acpHandoff keeps every entry and returns omitted: 0.
When entry text contains multiple closing conversation-so-far delimiters, buildChatHandoff escapes every occurrence before its own final closing line.

userStories.title: Append turns to the native chat document without failing sends
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Persist ACP message pairs in the native transcript with field-preserving load/merge/save and nonthrowing warning-only failure handling.

**Motivation** — The ACP backend stores only its ACP record and cost baseline there, never the messages (`packages/nax-agent-acp/src/client/backend.ts` `saveBaseline` / `saveFinal`), so nobody owns an ACP brain's message history yet.

**Approach** — Append messages to the native chat document: load, then save `{ ...doc, savedAt, messages: [...doc.messages, ...messages] }`, or `{ savedAt, messages }` when there is no document. Never throws: a load or save rejection is logged with `getLogger().warn("chat", "could not record the ACP turn", { sessionId, error: errorMessage(error) })`.

The native brain needs no change. The native backend already carries history across models (`carryHistoryAcrossModels: true`, `transcript-identity.ts` keeps another model's document), and a document with no `backend` field reads as native (`checkBackendKind`). A session started on an agent gets a native document created by the recorder (`{ savedAt, messages }`), so a later switch to a native model resumes it rather than creating a new session.

**Scope** — In: new `packages/nax/src/chat/acp/acp-transcript-append.ts` and its tests; inject now for deterministic ISO savedAt and use existing logger/errorMessage helpers. Out: message conversion (US-001), wrapper delivery (US-005), invoking append and await-before-completion (US-006), choosing the root transcript store and opener integration (US-007). Writing ACP turns into the agent's own transcript document under `acp-<agent>/`; that document keeps only the ACP record and cost baseline. Retrying, or showing in the TUI, a failed recording; it is logged as a warning only.

**Interface** — verbatim TypeScript:
```ts
/**
 * Append messages to the native chat document: load, then save
 * `{ ...doc, savedAt, messages: [...doc.messages, ...messages] }`, or `{ savedAt, messages }` when
 * there is no document. Never throws: a load or save rejection is logged with
 * getLogger().warn("chat", "could not record the ACP turn", { sessionId, error: errorMessage(error) }).
 */
export function appendNativeTurn(
  store: TranscriptStore,
  sessionId: string,
  messages: readonly ChatMessage[],
  now?: () => Date,
): Promise<void>;
```
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] AC-1: appendNativeTurn(store, "s1", [u, a]) with no stored document saves a document with exactly the keys savedAt and messages.
[unit] AC-2: When store.load("s1") returns null, appendNativeTurn(store, "s1", [u, a]) saves a document whose messages is [u, a].
[unit] AC-3: With no stored document, appendNativeTurn(store, "s1", [u, a], now) saves savedAt equal to the injected now() as an ISO string.
[unit] AC-4: With a stored document holding messages [m1], appendNativeTurn saves messages [m1, u, a].
[unit] AC-5: appendNativeTurn saves a stored document's model unchanged.
[unit] AC-6: appendNativeTurn saves a stored document's owner unchanged.
[unit] AC-7: appendNativeTurn saves a stored document's turn unchanged.
[unit] AC-8: appendNativeTurn saves a stored document's instructionSources unchanged.
[unit] AC-9: appendNativeTurn calls store.save once, with "s1" as the session id.
[unit] AC-10: When store.save rejects, appendNativeTurn resolves.

[unit] AC-11: When store.save rejects, the logger's warn (observed with spyOn(getLogger(), "warn") or a sink added with addSink) is called with "chat", "could not record the ACP turn" and data whose sessionId is "s1".
[unit] AC-12: When store.load rejects, appendNativeTurn resolves and store.save is not called.
[unit] AC-13: When store.load rejects, the logger's warn (observed the same way) is called with "chat", "could not record the ACP turn" and data whose sessionId is "s1".
[unit] Failure handling: When store.load or store.save rejects with an error, appendNativeTurn logs warning data whose error is errorMessage(error).

routing.reasoning: One small additive helper uses the existing TranscriptStore and logger to load/merge/save inside a catch, with an injected clock; persisted session documents still require the mandated session security override.

suggestedCriteria: When a stored native document has schemaVersion, backend and instructionDirectories fields, appendNativeTurn preserves those fields unchanged.
When appendNativeTurn appends a pair, the original loaded document and its messages array remain unchanged.

[unit] AC-2: When the wrapped iteration yields only turn_end { status: "errored", output: "" }, appendNativeTurn is not called and the next send("again") is still prefixed with "H\n\n".
[unit] AC-3: When the wrapped iteration throws before turn_end, appendNativeTurn is not called.

[unit] AC-4: With handoff: "H" and a wrapped send yielding text_delta "ok" and turn_end, _acpRecorderDeps.appendNativeTurn is called once with the store, the session id and acpTurnMessages({ message: "hi", events, acp }), where events are the yielded events (the user message is "hi", not the prefixed text).
[unit] AC-5: A turn with agent work ending turn_end { status: "errored" } is recorded (appendNativeTurn is called once).
[unit] AC-6: When a turn reaches turn_end and its only work is a non-empty thinking_delta, recordAcpTurns calls _acpRecorderDeps.appendNativeTurn once.
[unit] AC-7: When appendNativeTurn returns a promise that resolves later, the consumer's for await over send("hi") does not finish before that promise resolves.

[unit] Failure handling: When a worked turn ends cancelled, timed_out, interrupted or errored, recordAcpTurns appends the same message pair acpTurnMessages produces for that status, including reply-so-far text or the status-specific no-reply placeholder for thinking-only work.
[unit] Failure handling: When a terminal turn contains only empty text_delta, empty thinking_delta and non-work updates, recordAcpTurns leaves the handoff pending for the next send.

[unit] Failure handling: When the native store's load or save rejects during a worked terminal send, consuming recordAcpTurns.send completes normally with every original event delivered unchanged and in order.

routing.reasoning: Extend the existing wrapper by composing upstream message conversion and nonthrowing append through one deps seam, awaiting persistence after a worked terminal iteration; session persistence requires strict test isolation.

suggestedCriteria: When a turn's only agent work is a tool_call followed by turn_end, recordAcpTurns records the tool summary and sends the next message without the pending handoff.
When two terminal worked turns are consumed sequentially, recordAcpTurns appends each original user/assistant pair once in conversation order.

userStories.title: Carry conversation history into and out of ACP chat brains
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Integrate unseen-history handoff and ACP recording into openChatSession and remove obsolete cross-brain history-loss notices.

**Motivation** — User ruling 2026-10-29 (design §6.4): history carries over on a switch, in every direction (native to ACP, ACP to native, ACP to another ACP agent), the same experience as switching native models today.

**Approach** — `openAcpBrain` also reports whether the agent session is fresh (created, with or without the fallback). The ACP branch computes `unseenMessages(history.messages, acp.agent, fresh)`, then `acpHandoff(...)`, renders it with `buildChatHandoff`, and returns `session: recordAcpTurns(opened.session, { store: transcripts, sessionId: meta.sessionId, acp, handoff })`. Its `notice` is the fallback notice and `ACP_HANDOFF_TRIMMED_NOTICE(label, omitted)` (when `omitted > 0`), joined by `"; "` when both exist, undefined when neither does. When neither exists the handle has no `notice` key at all (the existing `open-chat-session-acp.test.ts` asserts `"notice" in handle` is false). The `ChatSessionHandle.notice` doc comment is updated to cover the trimmed-handoff case. The native branch is unchanged and its session is not wrapped.

When the ACP branch opens an agent:
- a fresh agent session (no agent document, or the F2 fallback after an unusable one) has seen none of the native document;
- a resumed agent session has seen everything up to and including the last assistant message whose `origin.provider` is `acp:<that agent>`; it has not seen what follows. With no such message (a session from before this feature), it has seen none.

The unseen messages become handoff entries (`acpHandoff`), rendered by the new prompt builder `buildChatHandoff`, and the wrapper puts that text in front of the first message it sends: `<handoff>\n\n<message>`. ACP sends the session's system instructions only on the first prompt of a new session (`instructionsSent` in `backend.ts`), so a fresh agent receives instructions, then the handoff, then the message; a resumed one receives the handoff and the message.

The native brain needs no change. The native backend already carries history across models (`carryHistoryAcrossModels: true`, `transcript-identity.ts` keeps another model's document), and a document with no `backend` field reads as native (`checkBackendKind`). A session started on an agent gets a native document created by the recorder (`{ savedAt, messages }`), so a later switch to a native model resumes it rather than creating a new session.

The new ACP-branch logic (unseen messages, handoff, wrapping, notice) goes in a small helper in `open-chat-session.ts` rather than inline in `openChatSession`, which `check:complexity` already scores at 11 of 20. `packages/nax/src/chat/chat-host.ts` is at 593 of 600 lines and is not changed: all wiring sits in `open-chat-session.ts` (342 lines) and five new modules under `src/chat/acp/`.

The brain-change notice goes. `useSwitchNotices` no longer adds `<new> does not see <old>'s turns`; a model change shows only `model: <name>`, as for a native model change. `modelNotices(to)` takes only the new model and returns only `model: <name>` (the call site passes only `model`); `brainOf` and the then-unused `parseChatAcpModel` import are removed (build gate).

**Scope** — In: modify `packages/nax/src/chat/open-chat-session.ts`, `packages/nax/src/chat/acp/index.ts` (re-export public names from history, handoff entries, handoff, transcript append and recorder beside existing exports), and `packages/nax/src/tui/chat/use-switch-notices.ts`. Update the `US-011 useSwitchNotices brain changes` AC-10, AC-13 and AC-14 expectations in `packages/nax/test/ui/chat/acp-labels.test.tsx` to the single notices `["model: Codex"]`, `["model: gpt-6[high]"]`, `["model: Claude Code"]`; retain same-agent and native effort expectations. Add the two specified integration test files. Out: reimplementing helper algorithms (US-001–006), changing `chat-host.ts`, the native backend, nax-agent or nax-agent-acp, and showing handoff text in the TUI transcript. Handing history to an agent through its own history import (`session/load` replay or an agent-specific API); the handoff is text in front of the first prompt. Writing ACP turns into the agent's own transcript document under `acp-<agent>/`; that document keeps only the ACP record and cost baseline. Updating `.nax/mono/packages/nax/context.md`, which is read-only to the run; a manual follow-up after merge.

**Interface** — Existing entry points and target return contract:
```ts
openAcpBrain(request, { meta, acp }, deps): Promise<OpenedBrain>
```
OpenedBrain continues to contain session and optional notice and additionally reports a boolean fresh. ChatSessionHandle retains session/meta/release/history and optional notice, with no notice property emitted when neither fallback nor trimming occurs.

Seams: US-007 consumes `recordAcpTurns` (US-005, US-006), `acpHandoff` (US-003), `buildChatHandoff` (US-003) and `unseenMessages` (US-002). Entry point: `openChatSession` on an `acp:` model, which `ChatHost.start`, `switchTo` and `resume` reach through the host's opener. The ACs that check the first prompt, the resumed suffix and the recorded pair drive `openChatSession` and then the returned `handle.session.send`, and assert on what the stubbed agent session received and what the native store holds; the host-level AC enters one level higher, through `createChatHost(...).send`. Keep the real createFileTranscriptStore in the host-level test; stub only the session/backend seams, never launch a real ACP adapter. `runChatTurn` consumes the whole wrapper iterable before writing metadata, so store assertions immediately after host.send resolves must already see the pair. Verification note: `bun run typecheck` and `bun run check:all` stay green with `brainOf` and its import removed; these are pipeline gates, not additional acceptance criteria.
acceptanceCriteria: [integration] AC-1: openChatSession on acp:codex for a new agent session (no agent document), with a native document holding [user "plan it", assistant "ok"], returns a handle whose first session.send("go") calls the created agent session's send once with the single string argument buildChatHandoff(acpHandoff(those messages)) + "\n\n" + "go".
[integration] AC-2: On acp:codex with no native document, the first send("go") calls the agent session's send with "go".

[integration] AC-3: On acp:codex resuming the agent document, where the native document's last message is an assistant message with origin acp:codex, the first send("go") calls the agent session's send with "go".

[integration] AC-4: On acp:codex resuming the agent document, with native messages [u1, a1 (origin acp:codex), u2 "native q", a2 "native a"], the first send is prefixed with the handoff of [u2, a2] only.
[integration] AC-5: When resuming the agent document fails with AGENT_SESSION_NOT_FOUND (the F2 fallback), the first send is prefixed with the handoff of every native message.

Goal and baseline: F3 extends merged F1/F2 so nax chat remains one conversation when switching native→ACP, ACP→native, or ACP→another agent, and recorded ACP turns reappear on resume. This is an enhancement, not greenfield. All implementation changes belong in packages/nax; the agent, ACP and AI packages are read-only references. Graph-first navigation was unavailable because this host exposes no codebase-memory MCP tools; findings below come from direct reads and text search. No implementation or test execution is part of this PRD task.

Existing opening architecture: packages/nax/src/chat/open-chat-session.ts:38 exposes _openChatSessionDeps for backend factories, session create/resume, transcript stores, time and UUID injection. ChatSessionHandle.notice currently describes only unusable-agent fallback at :74. Native sessionOptions already sets carryHistoryAcrossModels: true at :202. OpenedBrain at :217 currently has only session and optional notice; openAcpBrain at :226 uses a distinct file store under acpTranscriptDir, resumes if an agent document exists, retains unusable documents before a fresh create, and leaves unrelated failures propagating. historyOf at :277 reads only messages/savedAt. openNativeBrain at :282 loads the root native document and chooses create versus resume from its presence. openChatSession at :304 validates model input before taking the shared storage lock and has a separate ACP branch near :333 which loads native history then returns an unwrapped ACP session. Target: report fresh on ACP opens, factor the new ACP history/handoff/notice/wrapper integration into a small helper in this file, and retain existing native behavior and cleanup. The specification places this function at complexity 11/20; do not pile new branches inline.

Public contracts and import boundaries: packages/nax-agent/src/session/agent-session-types.ts:84 defines all five TurnEndStatus values; :103 defines SessionEventBody, including text_delta, thinking_delta, stream_reset, tool_call, tool_result and terminal turn_end; :176 defines AgentSession with optional runCommand, live id/backend/lastTurn, synchronous turn-slot claiming in send, answer/cancel/close. packages/nax-agent/src/session/agent-session.ts:71 implements the facade; its send at :102 rejects closed/busy synchronously before returning an iterable. A wrapper implemented as an async generator send would defer this and break compatibility: invoke inner send immediately and return a separate forwarding iterable. Getter delegation must not snapshot properties or eagerly require them on stubs. Forward methods with their original receiver. packages/nax-agent/src/native/session/transcript-types.ts:30 defines optional backend/owner/model/turn/instruction audit fields and messages; :51 defines load/save/retainFailed/delete/markTurn. Agent documents under acp-<agent>/ continue to own only ACP lifecycle/cost data, never copied history. No migration/backfill or one-time rewrite: an old resumed agent with no acp:<agent> origin marker receives the entire native history; a fresh or fallback-created agent also receives everything. Resumed agents receive only the suffix after their last assistant origin marker. Compaction can erase markers, causing acceptable repeated handoff. Recorded origin is per agent/model, not effort, and the last-seen scan is per agent rather than per model.

Resume origin markers and bounded handoff intentionally trade complete replay for bounded size and may repeat old context on prefeature sessions/compaction. outOfScope: Recording an ACP turn's tool calls as structured native `toolCalls` / `tool-result` messages, or carrying tool inputs, results or thinking; a turn's tools are recorded as one `[tool] <name>` line each.
Writing ACP turns into the agent's own transcript document under `acp-<agent>/`; that document keeps only the ACP record and cost baseline.
Recording a turn that throws or ends without `turn_end`.
Retrying, or showing in the TUI, a failed recording; it is logged as a warning only.
Native compaction that summarises away every message an agent wrote: that agent's next reopen is then handed the whole native history again, including turns it already saw.
An agent session opened before this feature has no recorded turns of its own, so its first reopen is handed the whole native history, possibly repeating what it saw.
Handing history to an agent through its own history import (`session/load` replay or an agent-specific API); the handoff is text in front of the first prompt.
Making the handoff bounds configurable; they are constants.

Recording, or clearing the handoff for, a turn the ACP backend counts as delivered (usage or plan updates only) but that showed no text, thinking or tool call; such a turn keeps the handoff pending and is not recorded.
A dedicated speaker for a native compaction summary (a user message starting with `COMPACTION_SUMMARY_PREFIX`); it is handed over as a `User:` entry.
Keeping UTF-16 surrogate pairs whole when an entry is cut at 4,000 units.
Showing the handoff text in the TUI transcript.
Changing `chat-host.ts`, the native backend, nax-agent or nax-agent-acp.
Workflow tools on the `nax-agent` ACP server that koda connects to; a separate later feature.
Updating `.nax/mono/packages/nax/context.md`, which is read-only to the run; a manual follow-up after merge.
